notes: Sweep claims mostly hold; corrections: (1) NVFP4 checkpoint is 186.9 GB on disk (safetensors total_size 186,891,034,892 B; 155 shards + nvfp4_act_scales), not ~180 GB — the 180.1B HF figure is the packed element count. Still fits 4x96 with ~197 GB (51%) spare and 7x96 with ~485 GB spare, well above the 15% KV floor. BF16 is 629.7 GB (too big for both nodes); community block-FP8 is 321.7 GB (fits 384 GB only with 16% spare, and see (5)). (2) Release: weights were public on HF 7-8 Aug 2026; 12 Aug is AA's listing date. (3) The NVFP4 repo ships only configuration_motif.py (no modeling_motif.py) and a proprietary direct-load tensor layout (2,439 keys vs 2,235 in BF16, no standard weight_scale suffixes) — it is loadable only by the vendor vLLM fork's MotifNvfp4MoEMethod; transformers cannot load it. (4) sm_120 status from the fork source: the Python guard is has_device_capability(100), a >= test that passes on cc 12.0; the CUTLASS FP4 grouped GEMM (csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/fp4/nvfp4_blockwise_moe_kernel.cu) has an explicit `version_num >= 120 && < 130 -> run_fp4_blockwise_scaled_group_mm_sm120` branch and CMake builds it for 12.0f under CUDA>=13 with ENABLE_NVFP4_SM120/ENABLE_CUTLASS_MOE_SM120 — so the vendor image (CUDA 13.1.1, arch list incl. 12.0+PTX) should contain a working sm_120 NVFP4 MoE path. Vendor validated NVFP4 only on 2x B200 and block-FP8 on H200; RTX PRO 6000 is untested — schedule a smoke test before the full run. Residual sm_120 risks: (a) GDLA sliding-window layers use a custom FlashAttentionDiffKV backend (asymmetric QK vs V head dims, head_size_v=128); fa_utils selects FA2 on cc 12.0 and whether vllm-flash-attn FA2 handles head_size != head_size_v on sm_120 is unverified; (b) the GDLA full-attention (MLA) layers fall to TRITON_MLA on cc 12.0 (FlashInfer-MLA/CUTLASS-MLA are SM100-only, FlashMLA/FA-MLA are SM90) — slower decode and the same class of issue that needed vllm_sm120_nope.py for GLM-5.3-Flash; (c) mHC uses optional tilelang kernels with a Triton fallback. (5) Block-FP8 in the fork is DeepGEMM-only (SM90/SM100), so the community FP8 checkpoint is NOT an sm_120 fallback — NVFP4 is the only viable format on this node; if the FP4 MoE kernel fails there is no plan B short of the 7x node in BF16 (629.7 GB does not fit 672 GB with KV headroom either). (6) Vendor recipe (2x B200): vllm serve --trust-remote-code --quantization modelopt_nvfp4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --dtype bfloat16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-model-len 262144 --block-size 128 --tool-call-parser motif --reasoning-parser motif + self-spec MTP; for 4x96 use TP=1/DP=4/EP (experts split 96 per GPU) or TP=4; the image env also sets VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn, EP_DISABLE_GIN=1. Pull the image with the existing pull_image.py flow (no source rebuild possible at v0.26.0). (7) MIT licence confirmed on Motif-3 and Motif-3-NVFP4 (LICENSE.md); the 'non-commercial' claim seen on some blogs applied to the Beta preview only. (8) AA-listed 260k ctx = 262,144 native.

notes: VERIFIED: repo exists (created 19 Aug 2026, card release date 31 Aug 2026, last modified 2 Sep 2026); base deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 created 31 Jul 2026 07:30 UTC, MIT, 'official release of DeepSeek-V4-Flash, superseding the preview'. SIZE: NVFP4 repo = 175.56 GB safetensors (48 shards); base 0731 = 166.89 GB. The sweep's '~160-170 GB' guess is wrong for the NVFP4 build: DeepSeek ships the routed experts natively in MXFP4 (config expert_dtype 'fp4', attention FP8), and NVIDIA's NVFP4 is a lossless bit-cast (same E2M1 nibbles, E4M3 scale per 16 replaces E8M0 per 32) of only the routed experts - attention, shared experts, head and mtp.* stay FP8, kv_cache_quant_algo null - so it is 8.7 GB LARGER than the base with identical weight bits (NVIDIA's own table: GPQA 91.5/91.5, AA-LCR 71.8/72.1, SciCode 52.1/51.7, TB2.1 73.7/74.7 vs source). FIT: 175.6/384 = 46% used, 208 GB spare (54%); 4-way TP ~44 GB weights per GPU; on 672 GB, 496 GB spare. KV is tiny (1 KV head x 512 dim, FP8) but the FP4 indexer cache is unavailable on sm_120, so budget an FP8/BF16 indexer cache. PARAMS: HF element count 304.18B, NVIDIA card '304B total, 13B activated'; AA's 284B is the marketed figure excluding MTP/DSpark heads - the sweep's 'element count 304B incl. MTP' is correct. Recommendation: download the base deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (166.9 GB, the validated sm_120 checkpoint, MXFP4 experts like your MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 run) first; take the NVIDIA NVFP4 build (175.6 GB) only if the sm_120 NVFP4 MoE kernel path beats the MXFP4 'auto' backend on your stack - same weights either way. IDENTITY CHECK for the 'DeepSeek-V4-Flash (measured, deleted)' entry: the April preview deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash is 290.94B elements (22 Apr 2026, AA ~40, no DSpark); 0731 is 304.18B elements with DSpark in-checkpoint and +10 AA points - if the deleted checkpoint was the April one, this is a different, materially stronger model; if it was 0731, verdict becomes already-have. Newer DeepSeek releases: V4-Pro-0813 (1.65T, too big), V4-Flash-Vision-Exp (31 Aug, experimental multimodal, text parity, no official quant) - neither supersedes 0731 for text benchmarking.

notes: CORRECTIONS TO THE SWEEP: (1) 'Native FP8 = 304.6B elements (~305 GB, tight on 4x)' is wrong. config.json sets expert_dtype "fp4": routed experts are natively MXFP4 (ue8m0 scales), only attention/dense/shared/DSpark are FP8, ViT is BF16. The official repo is 48 safetensors shards = 167.8 GB (156.3 GiB) — essentially the same as V4-Flash-0731 (166.9 GB) that you already measured and deleted. The 306.8 GB AtlasCloud FP8-DSpark repo is an FP8 upcast of the FP4 experts for FP4-less hardware, not the native format. (2) The community NVFP4 builds (s-zaizen 176.5 GB, msuiche 176.5 GB, both ModelOpt, experts-only W4A4, everything else kept FP8/BF16) are LARGER than the native checkpoint (NVFP4 e4m3 per-16 scales vs MXFP4 e8m0 per-32) and are lossless casts of the same 4-bit experts, so no quality gain. They target SM100/SM121: msuiche tested on B200 with flashinfer trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe and needs strip_vision.py on stock vLLM v0.28.0 (text-only); s-zaizen tested on 2x DGX Spark GB10 (sm121) with a vLLM fork. In vLLM's deepseek_v4 nvidia path an NVFP4-expert checkpoint (moe_quant_algo NVFP4) requires the nvfp4_cutedsl megakernel, and the DeepGEMM MegaMoE path raises 'requires SM100 GPUs' — no sm_120 route. On the RTX PRO 6000 use the NATIVE checkpoint: vLLM routes fp4 experts through Mxfp4MoEMethod / select_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_moe_backend whose backend enum includes B12X_MXFP4_MXFP8 / B12X_MXFP4_BF16, Marlin and Triton fallbacks (same MXFP4 family as gpt-oss-120b already on the box), with the FlashInfer sparse-MLA SM120 attention class. (3) Parameter framing: HF's 304.6B element count = ~284B language model (13B active; DeepSeek/AA headline) + 3 DSpark/nextn layers (~19B; 0731 has 1 layer and reports 290.9B) + ~0.5B ViT/aligner. Use 168 GB, not 305B, for VRAM planning. (4) Dates: API launch 21 Aug 2026 (api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news260821, API-only, images billed at <=384 tokens); HF weights 31 Aug 2026 06:16 UTC under MIT; AA page (release 21 Aug, 'proprietary', 284B) is stale on the open-weights status. (5) Benchmarks: Terminal-Bench 2.1 83.9 CONFIRMED from the official card (0731: 82.7; Opus-4.8: 85.0); NL2Repo 57.7, DeepSWE 59.3, Toolathlon-Verified 75.9; DeepSeek states text-only agent performance is 'comparable' to 0731 — the real delta is multimodal (ApexBench 36.5 vs 26.2, ZeroBench 35.0). NOT VERIFIED (web-search budget exhausted): '#14 overall / 2nd-best open on llm-stats mirror' and 'GDPval-AA 1666' — the llm-stats Terminal-Bench page reachable was the old TB1 board without this model. (6) Fit: 167.8 GB on 384 GB = 44% (~42 GiB/GPU at TP=4), >55% free for KV — comfortably over the 15% bar; vLLM's recipe notes 1M-token KV needs far more memory than the weights and benchmarks at --max-model-len 32768 with --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 (--enable-expert-parallel on GB200). On 672 GB it fits trivially but TP=7 is awkward (256 experts, 64 index heads) — run TP=4(+EP) on 4 of the 7 GPUs or add PP. (7) Engine reality on sm_120: vLLM v0.28.0 serves it TEXT-ONLY (arch string DeepseekV4ForCausalLM matches; vision.*/aligner.*/image_* tensors must be stripped — msuiche's strip_vision.py) with DSpark; image input needs vLLM main >= 2 Sep or the deepseekv4-flash-vision image, which has no published run on anything but GB200 (vision path 'untested' on H200/B200/B300, nothing on sm_120). SGLang 0.5.18: text class + DSPARK, native FP4 experts by default; cookbook recipes for 'Flash Vision' were merged 31 Aug-2 Sep (B200/GB300; DGX Spark FP4 cell PR #37737 still open) but SGLang has no ViT or image processor, so text-only; whether the 22-Aug 0.5.18 wheel tolerates the extra vision tensors is unverified (loader has 'name not in params_dict' guards that may skip them). (8) Practical read: this is a re-download of the 168 GB V4-Flash you already measured; add it for the vision capability and because it is DeepSeek's current Flash checkpoint, expecting text results within noise of 0731.

The 103.8B 'Parameters' figure undercounts bytes because hf_quant_config excludes lm_head, layers 0-2 entirely, and every layer's self_attn, share_expert and moe.gate (all left BF16), plus the ViT, and NVFP4 carries FP8 block scales at group_size 16. ENGINE CAVEATS: HF card is custom_code (trust-remote-code). Official vLLM NVFP4 recipe: --quantization modelopt --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 4 --reasoning-parser step3p5 --tool-call-parser step3p5 --async-scheduling; note it uses --max-model-len 8192 and omits the MTP flag, though the GitHub README says the latest NVFP4 checkpoint supports vLLM MTP spec-decode. The FP8/BF16 recipes say --disable-cascade-attn and TP8. SGLang's NVFP4 recipe depends on --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm and --attention-backend trtllm_mha (datacenter-Blackwell kernels); given the team's prior finding that GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4 did not work on SGLang on sm_120, expect vLLM to be the viable path, and the sm_120 NVFP4 MoE kernel selection (b12x-style linear backend finding) is unverified for this arch. vllm_arch_supported: yes — Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration is native in the vLLM registry (LoRA + PP); Medium-3.5-specific fixes (Mistral tokenizer chat_template #41658, streaming tool calls #41730, Pixtral processor #41948) merged May 2026 before v0.22.0 (29 May), and v0.23.0 made Model Runner V2 default for Mistral dense models, so v0.28.0 (latest, 26 Aug 2026) covers it. SGLang 0.5.18: architecture registered (srt/models/mistral.py EntryClass includes Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration, day-zero PR #23849 27 Apr 2026, cookbook PR #31507 17 Jul) but issue #29835 "Mistral-medium-3.5 does not start since 0.5.13" (AttributeError 'str' object has no attribute 'get_quant_method') is still OPEN; probable fix PR #29111 (init-arg forwarding) merged 25 Jun so should be in 0.5.15+, unconfirmed. Treat vLLM as the safe path.
mtp_or_drafter: No MTP head (dense model). Official EAGLE drafter: mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-EAGLE (created 27 Apr 2026, single consolidated.safetensors 3.07 GB in Mistral format, ~1.5B params BF16), documented for vLLM with speculative_config {"method":"eagle","num_speculative_tokens":3}; plain EAGLE, not EAGLE-3; no acceptance/speedup figures published and no vLLM issue found either confirming or breaking it. No community EAGLE-3 or DSpark drafter exists on HF (searches for "Mistral-Medium-3.5 eagle" and "draft" return only the official repo).
superseded_by: none as of 2026-09-03 — mistralai org newest repos are Shieldstral-1.0-3B (16 Jul) and Leanstral-1.5-119B-A6B (1 Jul, Lean prover); mistral.ai/news through 24 Aug 2026 has no Medium 3.6 / Large 4 / Devstral 3; AA open-source board lists only Mistral Medium 3.5 for Mistral. Mistral Large 3 675B (Nov 2025) is older and too big.
notes: Repo confirmed (956K downloads, updated 15 Jul 2026; HF Parameters 127,704.2M, tags fp8/mistral3; created 31 Mar 2026 private, public ~27-29 Apr: EAGLE + unsloth mirrors 27 Apr, bartowski 29 Apr, AA release date 29 Apr — sweep's 30 Apr is a day off). Model card: "Dense 128B parameters", 256k context, text+image in, reasoning toggle is two-level ('none'/'high') not multi-level; SWE-Bench Verified 77.6% and tau3-Telecom 91.4% confirmed; replaces Mistral Medium 3.1 + Magistral in Le Chat and Devstral 2 in Vibe (matches sweep). CORRECTION to sweep: the native FP8 checkpoint is 133.6 GB on disk (model-0000x shards 49.8+49.8+34), not ~128 GB, because vision tower/projector/lm_head/embeddings stay BF16; the repo also carries a duplicate 133.6 GB consolidated (Mistral-format) copy — download only one layout (repo total 267 GB). Best sm_120 quant: nvidia/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-NVFP4 (ModelOpt v0.44.0, 30 Jun 2026, 10 shards, 95.1 GB, 83.8B elements): MLP of decoder layers 4-86 in NVFP4, layers 0-3 and 87 MLP plus ALL attention linears kept FP8, KV cache FP8; accuracy within 0.1 pt of FP8 (MMLU-Pro 82.20 vs 82.31, GPQA-D 76.80 vs 76.88, AIME25 88.75 vs 88.85, SciCode 42.6 vs 42.5); NVIDIA validated TP=4 --max-model-len 196608 on B200. Alternative: NeuralNotwerk/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-NVFP4 (compressed-tensors, 30 Apr, 80.4 GB, 144.8K downloads, more layers quantised, no accuracy table); RedHatAI ships only the FP8 (127.7B) mirror, no NVFP4. On sm_120 use the b12x linear backend per the internal NVFP4 finding. VRAM: NVFP4 95 GB leaves ~289 GB (75%) on 4x96, FP8 134 GB leaves ~250 GB (65%) — both far above the 15% bar; 7x node trivially. KV cost = 88 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 x 2 = 180 KB/token at FP8 KV (360 KB BF16), so a full 256K sequence is ~47 GB — roughly 6 full-context sequences alongside NVFP4 weights, hundreds at 16-32K. Recommended vLLM flags from the card: --tool-call-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mistral (card still says "vllm nightly" — stale April text). Open vLLM issue #42354 (2-node TP=2 hang) is multi-node only. Capability caveat: AA 30 is far below GLM-5.3-Flash (57) and Qwen3.8-27B (52) already on the box; its value is as the Western dense-128B reference point and SWE-bench/agentic comparator, not an intelligence champion. Sources: hf.co/mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B (+config.json, tree), hf.co/nvidia/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-NVFP4 (+tree), hf.co/mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B-EAGLE (+tree), artificialanalysis.ai/models/mistral-medium-3-5, artificialanalysis.ai/models/open-source, mistral.ai/news, vLLM docs/models/supported_models.md + releases v0.22-v0.28, GitHub API issue search for vllm and sglang, sglang srt/models/mistral.py, sglang issue #29835 / PR #29111, sglang releases (v0.5.18 22 Aug 2026).

architecture: Dots3NoteForCausalLM (model_type dots3_note; DeepSeek-V3.2-derived: 46 layers = 1 dense + 45 MoE, 256 routed + 1 shared experts top-8 sigmoid/noaux_tc; 13 DSA sparse-MLA layers kv_lora_rank 512 index_topk 2048 + 33 SWA MLA layers window 513; 512K ctx; + 7B/1.2B-active MoE vision encoder, 0.8B Whisper-style audio encoder, 1.13B 1-layer MTP head)
aa_index: not listed on AA v4.1.1 (AA model page 404); BenchLM 68.67 = rank 25 overall, ~#4-5 open
vllm_arch_supported: yes - Dots3NoteForCausalLM + Dots3NoteMTPModel registered in vLLM v0.28.0 (26 Aug 2026), 0.28.1rc0, 0.29.0rc and main (absent in 0.27.x); code in vllm/models/dots3_note/nvidia/ reusing deepseek_v32. SGLang v0.5.18: NO (only main dots3.py/dots3_nextn.py + lmsysorg/sglang:dev-dots3-note image, PR #33829 under review).
mtp_or_drafter: Native MTP head (1 layer, 1.13B, layer 46 + eh_proj) present in FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints (NVFP4 keeps it BF16); vLLM --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}', SGLang NEXTN. No community EAGLE/DSpark drafter on the Hub.
notes: FACTS (HF API + GitHub API, 3 Sept 2026): dots-studio/dots3-note-prev (BF16, 576.9 GB) and -fp8 (298.7 GB, 133 shards) created 9 Aug, last modified 15 Aug 2026; GitHub studio-dots-ai/dots3-note-prev release commit 2026-08-13T16:46Z (sweep's 2026-08-14 is fine). HF 'Parameters' 288.4B = 280B LLM + 7B vision + 0.8B audio + 1.13B MTP. JANGQ-AI/dots3-note-prev-NVFP4 (17-20 Aug): modelopt NVFP4 group-16 on routed experts only; excludes self_attn, shared_experts, gate, layers.0 mlp, lm_head, vision, audio, layers.46/eh_proj (MTP) -> 186.2 GB on disk (card says ~174), HF element count 169.5B. VRAM: NVFP4 186/384 = 52% spare (46.5 GB/GPU at TP4) -> fits easily; FP8 299/384 = 22% spare (~75 GB/GPU) -> nominally passes 15% but tight and FP8 is the slow path on sm_120; 672 GB: NVFP4 72% spare, FP8 56% spare. KV is MLA so tiny: ~18 KB/token bf16 for the 13 DSA layers (incl. 128-d indexer cache) => ~4.8 GB per 262K sequence; SWA layers bounded by the 513 window. TP: 128 DSA heads / 64 SWA heads / 256 experts -> TP4 clean; TP7 impossible, 7x node would use TP4 or PP. Official recipe: vllm serve ...-fp8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend deep_gemm --max-model-len 262144 on 8xH100. SWEEP CORRECTIONS: (1) NVFP4 is ~186 GB not ~170; FP8 ~299 GB not ~288. (2) 'engine support unverified' -> now verified: vLLM 0.28.0 native incl. MTP; SGLang 0.5.18 does NOT have it. (3) 'custom arch' is really a DeepSeek-V3.2 derivative (Dots3NoteConfig subclasses DeepseekV3Config), so the DeepSeek-V4-Flash / GLM-5.3-Flash sm_120 work (vendor vLLM + vllm_sm120_nope.py) is the template; JANGQ validated it only on DGX Spark GB10 (sm_121) with a patched image ghcr.io/jjang-ai/dots3-note-gb10-vllm:sm121-cu130 that fixes sparse-attention decode, top-k indexing and NVFP4 GEMM - upstream sm_120 NVFP4 MoE + DSA decode is NOT verified. (4) Also takes video input. (5) BenchLM: 68.67, rank 25 overall; within the top-25 view the open models above it are Qwen3.8 Max 78.66, Hy4 preview 78.32, Qwen3.8-27B 71.97 (one extract also lists Qwen3.7 Max 71.40 as open) so it is #4 or #5 open on BenchLM; note Kimi K3/GLM-5.3/DeepSeek V4 Pro are absent from BenchLM's top 25, so BenchLM ordering does not track AA. (6) The 'open sibling of the IMO 2026 42/42 harness' claim appears nowhere on the model card or GitHub README - unsupported, treat as vendor/rumour. (7) Card benchmarks (vendor): SWE-bench Verified 78.4, SWE-bench Multilingual 75.7, Terminal-Bench 2.1 75.1. Not superseded: no newer dots3 repo on the Hub (dots-studio's latest are TTS models, 10 Aug), no final non-preview announced. Transformers support is still a PR (#47844). GGUFs exist (bartowski, ggml-org, DevQuasar, Baekpica) but irrelevant for vLLM.

notes: CONFIRMED: repo exists (created 2 Jul private, "Laguna S 2.1 initial release" commit 21 Jul 2026 17:03 UTC; GlobeNewswire + poolside.ai blog 21 Jul). Params 117,562M total per HF; model card says 8.5B active (press/blog round to 8B). Vendor benchmarks confirmed on the card: Terminal-Bench 2.1 70.2, SWE-bench Multilingual 78.5, SWE-bench Pro 59.4, DeepSWE 40.4, SWE Atlas 46.2, Toolathlon Verified 49.7. llm-stats TB2.1 mirror: rank 24 at 0.702 (Seed 2.1 Pro 0.710 above, Seed 2.1 Turbo 0.676 below; Hy3 71.7 on Poolside's own table) - sweep claim holds. Not on AA index - sweep claim holds. Not superseded: poolside HF org (33 repos) has nothing newer than S 2.1; only blog post after 21 Jul is the macOS Desktop Assistant (28 Jul); a larger Laguna is "beginning pre-training", unreleased. SWEEP ERRORS: (1) NVFP4 size is NOT ~65 GB: current checkpoint (weights replaced 1 Aug "Promote RC2->main", card updated 25 Aug) is 99.70 GB on disk (49 shards, total_size 99,697,287,856). Verified from quantization_config ignore list + safetensors headers: only routed experts in layers 1-39 are NVFP4; experts in layers 40-47 (ignore regex layers.4[0-7].mlp.experts) plus ALL attention q/k/v/o/g_proj, shared experts, router gates, layer-0 dense MLP and lm_head are BF16 (layer-47 expert tensors read as BF16 [3072,1024]). Arithmetic matches: 39x2.42B experts at 0.5625 B/param = 53 GB + 8x2.42B BF16 = 38.6 GB + ~8 GB BF16 rest. Poolside's README "roughly 71 GB" and the MiaAI-Lab RTX 6000 PRO repo (vLLM 0.25.1, ~71 GB, gpu-mem-util 0.78 on one 96 GB card) describe the pre-Aug-1 revision; the current NVFP4 no longer fits ONE 96 GB RTX PRO 6000 - needs TP=2 minimum on the 4x node. (2) FP8 is 131.27 GB, not ~118 (experts FP8 dynamic; attention/shared/lm_head BF16). INT4 99.69 GB; BF16 235.13 GB. FIT: 384 GB -> NVFP4 26% used (74% spare), FP8 34% (66% spare), even BF16 61% (39% spare); 672 GB trivial. KV is cheap: FP8 KV, 12 global layers = 24.6 KB/token (+~74 MB/seq constant for 36 SWA layers) -> ~6.3 GB/seq at 256K, ~25 GB/seq at 1M. sm_120 EVIDENCE: MiaAI-Lab/Laguna-S-2.1-DGX-Spark-RTX-6000-PRO ran NVFP4+DFlash on RTX 6000 PRO with vLLM 0.25.1: CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_120, --attention-backend FLASHINFER, kernels auto-select FlashInferCutlass; they warn --linear-backend flashinfer_b12x is broken on 0.25.1 - moot here anyway since every dense linear is BF16 and only the fused-MoE NVFP4 kernel matters, so expect a smaller NVFP4-vs-FP8 uplift than on GLM-5.3-Flash. Vendor recipe caveats: parsers --tool-call-parser poolside_v1 --reasoning-parser poolside_v1; DFlash needs --max-num-seqs 32 (crashes at 256 on 0.25.1) and recipe adds --moe-backend triton with DFlash (test whether that bypasses NVFP4 MoE kernels); no min_p under spec decoding; VLLM_BLOCKSCALE_FP8_GEMM_FLASHINFER=0 for FP8; quantized checkpoints ship at 1M ctx (edit rope factor 32 / attention_factor 1.3466 for 256K). Smaller full-NVFP4 community alternatives if MoE-only coverage disappoints (accuracy unvalidated, drafter pairing unverified): primitive-ai/Laguna-S-2.1-mixed-NVFP4-MXFP8 68.7 GB (Blackwell, 29 Aug), JasonW2025/Laguna-S-2.1-ModelOpt-NVFP4-W4A4-KVcal-vllm 69.1 GB, kkuspa/Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4-0804 71.9 GB. TRT-LLM >=1.3.0rc16 also supports it. Agentic-coding specialist, not a general-frontier candidate; expect it below GLM-5.3-Flash on a general index but it is the strongest sub-120B open agentic-coding model available.

SWEEP CORRECTIONS: (1) "expect ~560 GB NVFP4" - the actual sum of the 67 safetensors shards is 595,185,395,016 bytes = 595.2 GB decimal = 554.3 GiB; the sweep's 560 was really GiB. (2) "native INT4 ~594 GB -> NVFP4 is smaller" is wrong: the base INT4 repo (64 shards) sums to 595,177,988,208 bytes = 595.2 GB, byte-for-byte the same size. Both quantise ONLY the routed experts (hf_quant_config excludes lm_head, embed_tokens, all of layer 0, every self_attn*, every shared_experts*, vision_tower*; the INT4 ignore list is the same set) at 4.5 bits/param (INT4 g32 bf16 scales vs NVFP4 g16 fp8 scales) with attention/shared/dense/vision in BF16. NVFP4 wins on kernel path (b12x FP4 GEMM vs the -40% W4A16 route for compressed-tensors INT4) and it sets kv_cache_quant_algo FP8, not on size. (3) Fit: 384 GB node - no (weights alone 145% of VRAM). 7x node: 554.3 GiB / 669.1 GiB (7 x 97,887 MiB) = 82.8% -> 17.2% spare before CUDA graphs, activations, vision buffers and any drafter (~16% with DFlash); in the sweep's own decimal-672 GB convention it is 595.2/672 = 88.6% -> 11.4% spare, i.e. FAILS the >=15% rule. KV itself is cheap (MLA 576 dims x 61 layers x FP8 = 35 KB/token, ~9 GB per 256K sequence), so the pressure is weights, not KV; fits_672GB=true is a marginal pass at best. VRAM FIT: NVFP4 186 GB = 48% of 384 GB (52% spare); official FP8 299 GB = 78% of 384 (22% spare, also passes the 15% bar, ~21 GB/GPU free); KV is cheap thanks to MLA (13 DSA layers x 576 x 2 B ≈ 15 KB/token BF16, SWA layers capped at a 513-token window, plus a small indexer cache) so 262K ctx ≈ 4 GB per sequence; BF16 (577 GB) fails 384 and is 86% of 672 (<15% spare). NVFP4 QUALITY RED FLAGS (sweep did not catch): the voves README claims lm_head, embeddings, shared expert, gate/router, low-rank q/kv projections and 'first 3 dense + last 2 layers' were excluded, but the actual checkpoint contradicts this: layers 0-2 MLPs are weight_packed FP4 (5 packed tensors each), layer 3 self_attn.kv_a_proj_with_mqa / kv_b_proj / gate_proj are FP4, layer 39 mlp.shared_experts.down_proj is FP4, and layers 38-39 are fully packed (773-777 packed tensors). The config ignore list only covers norms, layers 0-2 self_attn, gate.weight and lm_head. The quantiser's own stated failure mode ('corrupts the router, shared expert, or the MLA projections collapses quality silently') is thus partially violated by its own artefact; no accuracy eval published; 237 downloads, 2 likes; HF '8-bit' tag is spurious (it is nvfp4-pack-quantized, group 16, static input global scales, no KV-cache quant). NVFP4 repo also lacks the two MTP layers (see mtp field). ENGINE COST: serving on sm_120 means cherry-picking a conflicted, unapproved PR onto the ported vLLM (GDN path is known-good from Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4; MLA needs the same nope/Triton-MLA treatment as GLM-5.3-Flash; NVFP4 MoE + linear_backend b12x untested with this arch anywhere). RECOMMENDATION: not stale and not too big, but capability is unverified and the vendor's own numbers place it below models already on the box, while engine support is PR-only on both stacks - defer/low priority until vLLM PR #47708 merges; if benchmarked anyway, prefer the vendor FP8 on the 7x node with PP (keeps MTP and avoids the questionable community quant) over the NVFP4.

notes: CONDITIONAL ADD, low priority, currently blocked on engine support - the sweep's characterisation is mostly right but several details need correcting. (1) Dates: HF repo created 31 Jul 2026 (sweep's date) but the public release is 3 Aug 2026 (README + arXiv 2608.01662 v1 'LongCat Sparse Attention'); last modified 4 Aug. (2) Params confirmed: HF Parameters 69,127.2M; vendor says ~3B active; 26 safetensors shards = 138.29 GB BF16. Note the ~31B-param n-gram embedding table (~63 GB BF16) dominates the checkpoint; only ~34B params are MoE experts. (3) Not superseded: it is the newest LongCat text model; LongCat-2.0 (1.78T-A48B, Jul 2026, same LSA arch) is the older flagship and far too big, and the 560B-A27B LSA model in the paper was not released. (4) Quantisation: sweep is right that there is NO NVFP4 and no vendor FP8 for the Sparse variant (FP8 exists only for the Jan-2026 dense Lite, 101.8 GB). What exists: Intel/LongCat-Flash-Lite-Sparse-MXFP4-CT-AutoRound (12 Aug 2026, compressed-tensors format 'mxfp4-pack-quantized', W4A4 group-32 on expert Linears only; attention, indexer, router, embeddings, n-gram table and MTP kept BF16) = 88.61 GB, i.e. a Blackwell-native format like the MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 already on the box, but no eval vs BF16 published. Plus GGUF (llmfan46) and MLX (mlx-community 4/6/8-bit) - irrelevant for sm_120 serving. (5) Fit: BF16 138.3 GB on 384 GB leaves 245.7 GB (64%) spare, ~34.6 GB/GPU at TP4; MXFP4 88.6 GB leaves 77% spare; both trivially fit 672 GB. KV is MLA (kv_lora 512 + rope 64 = 576 dims x 28 attention blocks ~ 32 KB/token BF16), so even a 1M-token context is ~32 GB plus ~2 KB/token indexer cache - the whole 1M window fits on the 4x node. (6) Engine support (the real blocker): vLLM 0.28.0 = no (see vllm_arch_supported). SGLang 0.5.18 (22 Aug 2026) = partial: LongCat-2.0 LSA support landed in v0.5.16 (PRs #30202/#30275, validated on 8xB300 FP8), but the vendor's own model card says support is via SGLang PR #32918 ('basic adaptations', opened 30 Jul, still OPEN on 3 Sep 2026, 'verified locally on 8xH20-3e only'). Grepping the v0.5.18 tag confirms its changes are absent: zero-expert contribution moved after the TP all-reduce (without it TP8 GSM8K drops 0.849 -> 0.674), n-gram weight-name remapping for oe_embed_tokensN/oe_embed_projN (needed to load this checkpoint), indexer-fusion disabled for RMSNorm k-norm (index_k_norm_type='rms'), and arch-aware DeepGEMM head padding (native 16 heads on SM100/SM120). So it needs SGLang main + PR #32918, not a release. (7) sm_120 risk: the vendor launch command uses '--nsa-prefill-backend fa3' (now a deprecated alias of --dsa-prefill-backend) - FA3 is Hopper-only; the other DSA backends are flashmla_sparse/_q8/_kv/_auto (sm90/sm100), trtllm (sm100), flashinfer_sparse_mla, tilelang, aiter (ROCm). No vendor or SGLang cookbook hardware list includes RTX PRO 6000 / sm_120 (the SGLang DSA cookbook pages for GLM-5.3-Flash list H100/H200/B200/B300/GB200/GB300/MI only), and the box's prior finding was that GLM-5.3-Flash DSA does not run via SGLang on sm_120. Positive signal: PR #32918 explicitly adds SM120 to the DeepGEMM paged-MQA-logits indexer path. Net: expect the same porting effort as GLM-5.3-Flash (vendor/PR engine + sm_120 sparse-attention kernel workaround), unverified. (8) Capability: the sweep's 'likely below the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B tier' is unverified - no AA score exists (the non-thinking predecessor scored 17). Vendor evals (non-thinking): SWE-Bench Verified 68.2 (dense Lite: 54.4), SWE-Bench Pro 40.6, SWE-Multilingual 59.3, TerminalBench 2.0 33.7, tau2-Telecom 95.2, BrowseComp 48.6, MMLU-Pro 79.2, GPQA-Diamond 69.5, AIME 2026 65.7, HMMT Feb 2026 40.5, LongBench-v2 52.5, AA-LCR 48.0, MRCR-8n 44.7 - strong agentic-coding numbers for 3B active (above gpt-oss-120b class on SWE-V), but as a non-thinking model its AA index will sit far below the 52-60 open-weight reasoning champions. (9) The sweep's 'custom arch (LongCat lib)' is imprecise: the repo has no custom modelling code (no custom_code tag); transformers main only has 'longcat_flash' (Chat) natively, so the only vendor-endorsed serving path is SGLang PR #32918. Evidence: https://huggingface.co/meituan-longcat/LongCat-Flash-Lite-Sparse ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01662 ; https://huggingface.co/Intel/LongCat-Flash-Lite-Sparse-MXFP4-CT-AutoRound ; https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32918 ; https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48302 ; https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53811 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm/v0.28.0/vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py ; https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/longcat-flash-lite

(3) Headroom on 672 GB: 90.5 GB (13.5%) without MTP, 80.0 GB (11.9%) with MTP — below the 15% bar in the task's GB units; in GiB (7 x ~95.6 GiB usable = 669 GiB) it is 128/118 GiB = 19%/17.6%, i.e. nominally passes. Not '~120 GB KV'. (4) PARALLELISM on 7 GPUs: 64 heads, 8 KV heads, 16 SWA KV heads and 256 experts are all indivisible by 7; vLLM's Inkling Lamport fused collective hard-raises unless TP in (2,4,8) (NCCL fallback via LAMPORT_RS_SCONV=0 but heads still must divide), sconv SWA cache asserts tp_size <= num_kv_heads. So a 7x node can only run this as PP=7 x TP=1 (vLLM impl is SupportsPP via make_layers/get_pp_group) → ~83-85 GB (78.8 GiB) of weights per 96 GB card, ~11-16 GiB per card left for CUDA context, graphs, prefill activations and KV. Global-layer KV is cheap (11 layers x 8 KV x 128 x bf16 = 45 KB/token ≈ 2.2M tokens per 100 GB) so KV is not the constraint; per-GPU overhead is. An 8-GPU node would be a clean TP=8 fit at ~72% VRAM. (5) sm_120 ENGINE RISK (biggest unknown): upstream vLLM 0.28.0 Inkling uses custom kernels — ops/fa4_rel_attention.py picks tml_fa4 sheared-rel-bias for capability.major in (10,11) and vllm_flash_attn.cute score_mod for major==9; RTX PRO 6000 is major 12 and matches neither explicit branch, so it either falls to the CuTe-DSL FA4 path (needs FA4 CuTe sm_120 support) or fails — expect a port on the scale of the team's GLM-5.3-Flash vllm_sm120_nope.py work. MoE goes through generic FusedMoEFactory with ModelOpt NVFP4 weights (the b12x linear_backend finding likely applies). SGLang recipes use --attention-backend fa4 and flashinfer_trtllm FP4 GEMM/MoE backends (sm_100-class); consistent with GLM-5.3-Flash, SGLang is unlikely to be the sm_120 path. Cookbook still names an 'inkling-support (inkling-cu13)' branch build even though v0.5.18 contains inkling.py. (6) Alternatives are worse: RedHatAI/Inkling-FP8-dynamic = 952.6B elements (~950+ GB); lightseekorg/Inkling-MXFP4 (527B elements) is AMD Quark/ROCm. (7) Priority: Inkling-Small-NVFP4 (156B elements, ~166 GB + 4.5 GB MTP, 32 heads → TP=4 on the 384 GB node) is already downloading and AA puts it within 1-2 points (40 vs 41/42); full Inkling adds ~1-2 AA points for a PP-only, sm_120-unported, sub-15%-headroom deployment. Verdict too-big for 384 GB; marginal-fail for 672 GB. Engine versions checked: vLLM 0.28.0 (26 Aug 2026) is current; SGLang 0.5.18 is current on PyPI.

(2) '4x marginal' is wrong: 4x RTX PRO 6000 = 4 x 97,887 MiB = 410.6 GB decimal, so weights alone are 95.6% of VRAM before CUDA context, activations, CUDA graphs or any KV cache; even if vLLM skips the MTP weights (spec decode off) it is ~373 GB = 91%. Crucially, on 7x the pruned model is dominated by the UNPRUNED NVFP4 GLM-5.3 (Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 or RadixArk/GLM-5.3-NVFP4, ~465 GB = 64.7% of 7x, ~35% headroom, stock vLLM, no patch, full AA-60 quality, MTP included) - the only reason to accept the pruning loss was 4x fit, which it does not deliver. The sweep's 'inference-optimization/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-0.2B-A0.2B-MTP' is NOT an extracted MTP head: it is a 164M-param synthetic llm-compressor test fixture, 'not intended for inference'. notes: VERDICT 'add' refers to the official FP8 reference only; the NVFP4 build of this model is already on the box. SWEEP CORRECTIONS: (1) RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 is 135.2 GB on disk (206 shards: 60.4B U8 = 120.8B NVFP4 expert params, 51.2B FP8 PLE table, 8.0B BF16 attention/GDN/QSA/shared/MTP/vision) = 125.9 GiB, which matches the box's '126 GB' NVFP4, so RadixArk is almost certainly the checkpoint already on the box, not a 'smaller build'; the sweep's 119.6 GB is the HF element count, not a size. (2) Official FP8 is 185.5 GB decimal / 172.8 GiB (174.5B F8_E4M3 + 5.5B BF16), so '180 GB' is close but a decimal-vs-binary blur. (3) inference-optimization MTP repo is a synthetic test fixture, not a drafter (see mtp field). (4) primitive-ai mixed NVFP4-FP8 is 183.7 GB (PLE kept BF16 = 102 GB), i.e. larger than RadixArk, not smaller; primitive-ai plain NVFP4 is 186.4 GB; Inferact NVFP4 182.8 GB (PLE BF16); MagneticLab 215.2 GB; local-inference-lab 105.9 GB uses a nonstandard model_type 'qwen3_8_flash_next' with only 92.7B elements (something dropped) - avoid. (5) Release: HF repos created 2026-08-24, public announcement / GitHub news line 2026-08-26 (AA also says 26 Aug). PARAMS: model card says 125B main + 51B n-gram PLE + 6B active; HF safetensors total 179.999B (includes ~4B MTP head and ViT), so 180B is correct. BF16 original is 360.0 GB. ENGINE: vLLM 0.28.x does not have the arch; you need 0.29.0rc1+/main or the qwen38-flash-next image. PLE CPU-offload PR #53899 (VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1, 51-95 GB host RAM) is still OPEN as of 3 Sep; #53896 states NVFP4 + PLE offload is not supported (mixed-checkpoint handling under review). PR validation: BF16/FP8/NVFP4 without offload on GB300/GB200/H200 at TP2/TP4/TEP4; #53899 thread reports tests on RTX PRO 6000 and L40S. On RTX PRO 6000 primitive-ai needed VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=triton (default CUDA GDN decode kernel stalls under concurrent load) and a connector_mrv2.py overlay for a PLE-offload CUDA-graph race. Only a Hopper LL-GEMM tuning table exists (commit 191cecd5), no sm_120 tuning. vLLM recipe 4-GPU FP8 command: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --reasoning-parser qwen3 (+ MTP speculative-config). Known issues: plain TP8 incompatible with FP8 on H200 (use TEP8), TP1 compile-OOM on GB300, PLE has no pipeline-parallel support. FIT: FP8 185.5 GB / 384 GB = 48% if the 51 GB PLE table is vocab-sharded across TP ranks; if it is replicated per rank at TP=4 the footprint is ~134 + 4x51 = 338 GB (88%), which breaks the 15% headroom - then use PLE CPU offload (needs #53899 build + ~100 GB host RAM) or TP=2. KV cache is small (36 GDN fixed-state layers + 12 sparse QSA layers), so the 15% rule is generous for context. 672 GB: fits either way (338/672 = 50%); BF16 360 GB also fits the 7x node but TP=7 does not divide 16 KV heads / 48 V heads, so run TP=4 (or 2) there. STALE CHECK: no newer Qwen model on HF (newest author releases: Qwen-Drive-1.0-4B 27 Aug, unrelated); the card calls this the 'experimental preview of the architecture that will underpin Qwen4', and Qwen4 has not shipped, so not stale.

model: Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B official NVFP4 DSpark + DFlash drafters
architecture: Drafters: Qwen3-style dense GQA (model_type qwen3; architectures Qwen3DSparkModel / DFlashDraftModel), 6 layers, hidden 2688, 32 heads / 2 KV heads, vocab 131072; DSpark has sliding_window 1024 + Markov fixup head (rank 512), DFlash is non-causal block-diffusion with block_size 8. Target: nemotron_h hybrid (Mamba-2 + latent MoE + attention) with built-in MTP layers.
vllm_arch_supported: yes - target NemotronHForCausalLM (nemotron_h) + NemotronHMTPModel (nemotron_h_mtp) and drafters Qwen3DSparkModel (qwen3_dspark) / DFlashDraftModel (qwen3_dflash) are all in the vLLM main registry; speculative methods dspark / dflash / mtp are in vllm/config/speculative.py (NemotronH with num_nextn_predict_layers>0 auto-selects mtp). NVIDIA's recipes pin vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1; v0.28.0 (26 Aug 2026) adds an adaptive DSpark token budget and DFlash2. SGLang: nemotron_h.py has NemotronHForCausalLM with latent-MoE + MTP, SpeculativeAlgorithm enum has DSPARK / DFLASH / EAGLE (MTP via EAGLE with the target ckpt as draft), and v0.5.18 (22 Aug 2026) ships the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning cookbook; NVIDIA's own SGLang recipe uses the lmsysorg/sglang:dev-nemotron3-5-lightning container.
mtp_or_drafter: Three options exist. (1) Built-in MTP head inside the Lightning checkpoint itself (Base-BF16 tagged mtp; vLLM auto 'mtp'; SGLang '--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-draft-model-path <same ckpt> --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6'; TRT-LLM decoding_type MTP) - zero extra download. (2) Official DSpark drafter (967M params, 1.35 GB, 240.3K downloads): vLLM '--speculative_config.model <DSpark> --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens 3' (5 on GB200); SGLang 'DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 3'; SPEED-Bench mean acceptance 3.75 at draft length 7 (coding 4.38, multilingual 4.55). (3) Official DFlash drafter (833M, 1.18 GB, 3.6K downloads): SGLang 'DFLASH --speculative-dflash-block-size 6' (B200) / 4 (H100, GB10); mean acceptance 3.16. Community: only MLX ports of DSpark (mlx-community DSpark-bf16, Sawfwair DSpark-MLX) and GGUFs carrying the MTP head; no third-party EAGLE/DSpark drafters.

ACCURACY: NVIDIA reports NVFP4 vs FP8 parity - MMLU-Pro 82.20/82.31, GPQA-D 76.80/76.88, SciCode 42.6/42.5, AIME25 88.75/88.85 (validated on B200, vLLM v0.21.0, TP=4). sm_120 note: nvidia build is ModelOpt format (hf_quant_config.json) with FP8 KV - use the project's proven vLLM NVFP4 linear backend; NeuralNotwerk build is the one with direct sm_120 validation. (c) Active params: card says 6.5B, Mistral blog says 6B (8B incl. embedding/output layers). AA index 20 confirmed. FIT: 74.6 GB = 19% of 384 GB (81% spare), 11% of 672 GB; even the default FP8 checkpoint (~120 GB) or the BF16 (~239 GB, axolotl-ai-co/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-BF16) fit 384 GB with >=15% headroom, so NVFP4 is optional here. FORMAT: the mistralai NVFP4 repo is mistral-native only (params.json, no config.json - HF discussions #4/#6 ask for HF format); vLLM auto-detects and loads it as PixtralForConditionalGeneration + MistralLarge3ForCausalLM (config converter maps MoE-with-shared-expert params.json to model_type deepseek_v3 / MistralLarge3ForCausalLM). Card's command: vllm serve ... --max-model-len 262144 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --attention-backend TRITON_MLA --tool-call-parser mistral --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser mistral. SM_120 RISK: TRITON_MLA grouped-decode kernel assumes kv_lora_rank=512 and fails for this model's 256 ("incompatible dimensions at index 1: 256 and 512") - issue #45031 closed 2026-08-23 with no fix PR referenced, and #40260 (filed against this exact NVFP4 repo on GB10/sm_121) is still open; FLASH_ATTN_MLA needs FA3 (Hopper only), so on RTX PRO 6000 plan on FLASHINFER_MLA, VLLM_MLA_DISABLE=1 (MHA fallback with larger KV, affordable with ~300 GB free) or the team's existing sm_120 MLA port used for GLM-5.3-Flash. #48855 (2026-07-17) enabled FA MLA prefill for Mistral Small 4 head dims. NVFP4 experts use the same compressed-tensors nvfp4-pack-quantized MoE path as GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 already served on the box; the b12x linear-backend trick does not apply to attention here because MLA projections are unquantised. SGLang's Triton MLA asymmetric-KV fix (#27369) is still open, so SGLang on sm_120 is also unverified. NOT STALE: no Mistral Small 4.1/5 on HF (mistralai org newest: Shieldstral-1.0-3B 2026-07-16, Leanstral-1.5-119B-A6B 2026-07-01 which is a Lean-prover fine-tune of the same 119B-A6B backbone, Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B 2026-03-31) and Mistral's news feed through 2026-08-24 announces no successor. notes: Verified: repo exists (created 28 Nov 2025, public announcement 2 Dec 2025, Apache-2.0, 46K downloads); 273 safetensors shards totalling 389,945,893,880 bytes = 389.95 GB = 363.0 GiB. SWEEP CORRECTIONS: (1) checkpoint is ~390 GB, not ~370 GB — 363 GiB of weights against 4 x 97,887 MiB = 382 GiB usable leaves ~5% spare, far short of the 15% KV/activation headroom rule, and per-GPU TP=4 share is 90.8 GiB of 95.6 GiB, so it does NOT fit the 4x node at all, not even 'marginally'. (2) 'Not on the v4.1.1 index because it pre-dates it' is wrong: AA scores it 16 on v4.1.1 — below gpt-oss-120b (24), Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (24), Mistral Medium 3.5 (30) and MiniMax-M3 (45), i.e. nowhere near the frontier; it is a Dec-2025 non-reasoning model and Mistral's promised reasoning version never shipped as open weights. (3) The release date in the sweep (2025-11-28) is the HF repo creation date; public release was 2025-12-02. (4) 'Fits 7x': capacity yes (363 GiB / ~669 GiB usable = 54%, ~46% spare), but TP=7 is impossible (128 attention heads and 128 experts are not divisible by 7); viable topologies are TP=2 x PP=3 on 6 GPUs (60.5 GiB weights/GPU, ~35 GiB free each) or PP=7 / TP=1 — both lower throughput than a clean TP setup. (5) vLLM's official recipe warns NVFP4 shows a quality drop above 64K context and recommends FP8 for long context; the FP8 checkpoint (~675 GB) does not fit either node. (6) The 'largest Apache-2.0 MoE from a Western lab' and 'first-party EAGLE drafter, 256K ctx' claims are correct. Recommendation: do not download; if a Mistral entry is wanted, benchmark Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B (FP8 ~128 GB, single-node TP=4, EAGLE available, AA 30) instead, or Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603-NVFP4 for a cheaper slot. (3) The REAP-50 build is the WRONG pick for 384 GB: the 50% expert prune (256->128) was forced by a 16 GB card, its pruning cost is unablated (author's own caveat), its SWE-bench Verified 26/50=52% was context-limited at 49K, and its NVFP4A16 scheme is weight-only — vLLM selects MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel (dequant to bf16), i.e. the W4A16 path that project memory records as -40% on sm_120. notes: VERDICT RATIONALE: the model itself (Qwen3.8-27B, AA 52) is already on the box and measured, so this is a quant/drafter swap, not a new model. The swap is cheap (20.56 GB + 3.9 GB) and worth doing: QUASAR is the only build that is (a) all-linear NVFP4 W4A4 g16 — 24.35B params in FP4 including attention and gated-DeltaNet projections, vs unsloth/RedHat (23.42 GB) which keep ~10.6B params in FP8 (BF16 1.76B + F8_E4M3 10.62B + packed U8 7.49B) with only MLP in NVFP4, and RadixArk (attention FP8, MLP NVFP4) — so on sm_120 with the b12x backend more GEMMs hit FP4; (b) quantisation-aware-distilled (1 epoch, lr 1e-6, 2,446 steps against frozen BF16 teacher; arXiv 2608.13966 'QUASAR: Lowering the Loss Floor of QAT with Loss-Aware Reconstruction', Counathe/Athiwaratkun/De Sa/Zhang, submitted 14 Aug 2026); (c) retains the MTP head. lm_head, embeddings, visual, MTP are BF16; kv_cache_scheme null (use engine-side FP8 KV). Card requires vLLM >= 0.27 and says 'compute capability 10.0+' — sm_120 works via the compressed-tensors path you already use. CAVEATS / SWEEP CORRECTIONS: (1) 'should beat the PTQ builds' is self-reported by the quantiser: GPQA-Diamond 0.909 vs BF16 0.914 vs unsloth 0.894 vs Inferact 0.876; AIME26 1.00 vs 1.00 vs 0.978 — n=198 and n=30, so the 1-2 pt deltas are within sampling noise; the paper's own results are Qwen3/Llama-3.1 at 2-4 bit with the big gains at 2-bit (4-bit KL gain '>=10%') and it never evaluates Qwen3.8-27B. Being W4A4 on the DeltaNet/attention projections it is a MORE aggressive quant than the on-box builds; measure before adopting. (2) release_date 2026-08-23 in the sweep is the quant repo's creation date, not the model's (base: 5/14 Aug 2026). (3) HF 'Parameters' for this repo is 27.78B because HF unpacks compressed-tensors NVFP4 (BF16 3.43B + U8 24.35B); the params≈GB heuristic misfires — true size is 20.56 GB (BF16 6.86 + packed FP4 12.18 + FP8 scales 1.52). (4) DFlash2 is loaded in vLLM 0.28.0 under method 'dflash' (arch DFlash2DraftModel registered) — there is no separate 'dflash2' method; SGLang 0.5.18 cannot load DFlash2DraftModel at all (main only), so the maurienne-ai RTX-5090 drafter is unusable on the pinned SGLang and gives only +6% tok/s anyway. (5) The NInfer repos the sweep cited (neroued/Qwen3.8-27B-nvfp4-NInfer, splickz/qwen3.8-27b-yarn-nvfp4-sm120, MirkoCovizzi/…-NInfer) are NInfer-engine checkpoints (library: ninfer), not vLLM/SGLang-loadable; splickz has 1 like, 0 listed downloads, created 2 Sep, tagged 'reproduction' — drop. (6) RadixArk/…-NVFP4-BF16-LMHead (23.75 GB, ModelOpt, tested 4x GB300 SGLang) and gittensor LMHead4 exist as claimed but offer no QAT; gittensor RTX5090 base drops the MTP head. Other sweep facts check out: 89 likes; incoai 235K dl / z-lab 263 likes; incoai and z-lab are byte-identical mirrors (same config, both 18/15 Aug). FIT: 20.56 GB target + 3.9 GB drafter on 384 GB leaves ~94% spare; runs on a single 96 GB GPU with full 262K context. Recommended trial: vLLM 0.28.0, QUASAR target, compare (i) qwen3_5_mtp k=3, (ii) dflash with incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 k=7, (iii) the existing DSpark, against the unsloth/RedHat NVFP4 build on the same eval subset.

It also requires a custom modelopt_mixed SGLang image (ormandj/sglang-glm53-flash-sm120:v0.1.1 — Docker Hub repo returns 404, unverified) and will not load in stock vLLM/SGLang/transformers. (5) nota-ai NVFP4 is 205.6 GB / 386 shards with no sm_120 recipe — skip. LibertAIDAI is 181.2 GB but ModelOpt weight-only NVFP4-A16 (routed experts only), validated on GB10 sm_121 and H100/B200, not RTX PRO 6000; local-inference-lab NVFP4 (169B elems, calibrated A4 input scales, targets 4x RTX 6000) needs their vLLM fork dev/jovian-judgement; 0xSero EXL3 is exllamav3-only, irrelevant to the vLLM/SGLang stack. Best sm_120 quant: RedHatAI NVFP4 is true W4A4 (FP4 weights g16 + FP4 activations, compressed-tensors, vision/embeddings/head kept full precision), ships the MTP head, and its documented recipe is the vendor vLLM image with --tensor-parallel-size 4 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 plus MTP-5 spec config; 197.8 GB (190.2 GB without the MTP shard) leaves ~186 GB (48%) on 384 GB and ~474 GB on 672 GB — note KDA state cache, not KV, is the reported memory bottleneck. (3) The evidence repo's 'vLLM cannot serve this yet' is stale: vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next shipped 26 Aug and the arch merged to main 31 Aug. (4) garnermccloud build is named Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4-SSD-Stream (not -SSD); hn7305/-Spark is gated; local-inference-lab NVFP4 uses a non-standard model_type 'qwen3_8_flash_next' (92.7B elements, likely pruned/custom loader). '131B-A6B' pruned label not verified. Fit: 183.7 GB weights = 48% of 384 GB (>50% spare) and 27% of 672 GB; with PLE offloaded to host it serves on ONE 96 GB GPU at 88.8 GiB VRAM, needs ~100 GB free host RAM (or the NVMe pledisk overlay / FP8-INT4-NVFP4 PLE sidecars at 49/32/28.8 GB). Official FP8 = 172.8 GiB (fits 384 GB at TP4 with ~55% spare) but FP8-table checkpoints (official FP8, RadixArk, Inferact) cannot use the CPU-offload path on the shipped image. The 126 GB build already on the box is RadixArk NVFP4 (135 GB decimal; experts NVFP4 W4A4, PLE FP8-stored, everything else BF16, SGLang lane, validated GB300/B300 not sm_120). Why the primitive-ai mixed build is the sm_120 pick: measured on an RTX PRO 6000 with the stock vendor vLLM image — 84.4 tok/s single / 526 tok/s @32, +13% over its pure-NVFP4 sibling (74.4) and over FP8 baseline, accuracy statistically identical (92.2 knowledge, 84.8 tool-call); nota-ai calibrated NVFP4 measured slower (74.5). Required flags: --distributed-executor-backend mp, VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1, VLLM_PLE_OFFLOAD_READY_TIMEOUT=1800, and VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=triton (default CUDA GDN kernel deadlocks at ~32 concurrency with FP8 GDN projections); mount connector_mrv2.py to fix a startup shm race (#53960). MoE kernel on RTX PRO 6000 auto-selects FLASHINFER_CUTLASS; --moe-backend marlin is +10% single-stream, -1 to -3% @32 — relevant to your linear_backend/b12x finding. sm_120 caveats: vLLM recipe and SGLang cookbook validate only H200/B200/B300/GB300/MI355X; vLLM PR notes TP8 NVFP4 alignment failures (use EP) and >100K prefill hangs on GB10 sm_121. The DGX Spark SGLang guard hack (is_sm100_supported -> is_sm120_supported for the FlashInfer TRT-LLM QSA kernel) is confirmed but silently corrupts tokens past ~120K ctx; the Triton packed-varlen PR (36845) is the correct route — matches your GLM-5.3-Flash 'vendor vLLM not SGLang' pattern. Verdict is already-have because the model is on the box; recommend adding the primitive-ai mixed build (183.7 GB) as the vLLM/sm_120 serving path with MTP=3, keeping RadixArk for the SGLang lane.
